text:
acme-admin: Hey team — since last cert rotation our app's calls to our Redwood Private endpoint are intermittently failing with TLS errors. Started ~2h ago after we rotated certs. stack: nginx -> internal peering -> redwood.example.com:443. Error seen in logs: 

acme-admin: nginx logs: 
`[error] 1234#0: *5678 SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure) while SSL handshaking, client: 10.1.2.3, server: 10.2.3.4, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1"`

acme-admin: curl against endpoint from our bastion: 
`openssl s_client -connect redwood.private.acme:443 -servername redwood.private.acme -showcerts` 
shows the server presenting three certs but ordering looks odd: root first, then intermediate, then leaf. Some clients (our nginx+libressl build) fail validation if chain is not leaf->intermediate. Also seeing: 
`verify return:1
depth=0 CN = redwood
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`

emma (support): Bummer — thanks for the details and logs. Can you paste the full s_client output (showcerts) and the exact nginx error config? Also does this affect all of your hosts or only some? Any recent firewall/egress changes?

acme-admin: Pasting output (sanitized): 
````
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood
   i:/CN=Acme-Intermediate
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIID...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
 1 s:/CN=Acme-Intermediate
   i:/CN=Acme-Root
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIE...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
 2 s:/CN=Acme-Root
   i:/CN=Acme-Root
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIH...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
---
SSL handshake has read 4500 bytes and written 1234 bytes
---
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
````
We've not changed egress in last 6 months. A few hosts upgraded to nginx 1.23 with OpenSSL 3.1 recently. Problem seen from certain hosts consistently, others fine.

raj (infra): Quick thought — if cert bundle is served with root first, strict OpenSSL versions may fail. Also if OCSP/CRL fetching is blocked, clients that require AIA fetching may error. Can you check whether your hosts can reach the intermediate issuer's AIA/OCSP endpoints? Try: `curl -I https://ocsp.acme.example/` from failing host.

acme-admin: curl to ocsp.on our failing host returns `Connection timed out`. From a working host it resolves fine. Firewall team did some egress tightening last week but said they allowed the usual list — will check specific endpoints.

jen (sre-oncall): Important: some TLS stacks will succeed if the chain is ordered leaf->intermediate->root. If the server presents root first, verification may stop early and not try fetching issuer. Also if the client relies on AIA to download intermediates and egress is blocked, you'll get unable to get local issuer certificate. So looks like two issues: misordered bundle on server side AND egress block for OCSP/AIA.

cert-rotator-bot: Deploy of cert bundle for customer-acme completed at 2024-12-03T10:12:01Z on edge-2. Noted "bundle_bundle_order": "root-first" in deploy logs.

emma (support): Thanks bot + jen. acme-admin, two remediation paths: 
1) We can re-publish the cert bundle with proper ordering (leaf, intermediates, root optional). I can trigger a rotation with correct order — will need your approval and short maintenance window.
2) In parallel, ask your infra/firewall team to allow egress to the issuer's AIA and OCSP endpoints so clients can fetch missing intermediates.

acme-admin: Approve path (1). We'll also open a ticket for egress. Preferred window now +20m if possible. Impact: some traffic (~30% of requests) failing.

raj (infra): Emma — to re-push correct ordering I need the PEMs or we can reorder server-served bundle on our side. If you have the leaf + intermediate files, the correct concatenation is: `cat leaf.pem intermediate.pem > bundle.pem` (omit root or append root only if required). Many servers require leaf first.

emma (support): I can trigger a re-deploy using the existing certs but force ordering. Triggering now. Notifying ops.

cert-rotator-bot: Starting redeploy job id job-9921 for customer-acme at 1791234800. Applying cert bundle with ordering: leaf -> intermediate -> root.

acme-admin: Re-tested on failing host after ~60s: `openssl s_client -connect redwood.private.acme:443 -servername redwood.private.acme -showcerts` now shows leaf first, intermediate second, root last. Handshake succeeds, nginx log shows no SSL_do_handshake error.

acme-admin: Confirmed ocsp still blocked but OK for now because chain presented fully. Will still pursue allowing ocsp/AIA.

jen (sre-oncall): Great. We'll keep an eye on logs for 24h. Please collect any 5xx / TLS handshake failure spikes and paste here. Also if you see clients on older OpenSSL still failing, we'll investigate client side.

emma (support): Marking as resolved on our side pending your egress ticket. If you want we can add an automated check to validate bundle ordering post-rotation and warn customers.

acme-admin: Yes please — a warning would have saved us some hours. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jen (sre-oncall): Filed follow-up: ACTION-5421 — add bundle-order validation + egress docs for AIA/OCSP endpoints.

emma (support): Closing thread but will re-open if issue resurfaces.
